about: Trade practice the build follows where the documents are silent or wrong (Q6216): how each trade runs or places what the drawings leave out, and what the field installs where a drawn value can't be built. Order of authority: the documents, then the code (coderules.json and each trade's rules data, cited here where a rule uses a code number), then this file. Each rule: its id, the trade, what it fills in or corrects, its numbers, and its basis: the reason every object it lays in or value it corrects carries, so nothing it makes passes for drawn.

rules.fills: a roof level's framing where the roof plans name trusses or joists: the members across the roof's short way at their spacing, as deep as the notes say, bearing on the walls at the level's elevation (its top of plate or truss bearing), the deck on them, the outside walls carried up round them to the deck or the parapet (numbers: spacing_in and depth_in when a note gives none; chord_in, a member's width; deck_in, the deck and roofing over the members; min_span_ft, the shortest piece kept)
rules.basis: trade practice: pre-engineered wood roof trusses (and open-web joists) are set at 24" on centre across the building's short way, bearing on the outside walls' top plate, at least 24" deep for a flat or low-slope roof; the sheathing and roofing go on their top chords, and the outside walls (or a parapet) close the truss space round the edge

rules.fills: a ceiling luminaire's place where the electrical plan's symbol and the reflected ceiling plan's light differ (numbers: reach_ft, the farthest a light is moved; connect_reach_ft, a light this close is at its spot)
rules.basis: trade practice: the electrician sets each ceiling light where the architect's reflected ceiling plan draws and dimensions it, the ceiling's layout aligning lights, sprinklers and sensors; the electrical plan's symbols show which lights and circuits, not where to the inch

rules.fills: a fixture's cold or hot water branch, or a room's branches, no plan joins to a main (numbers: plumbing.json fill_in)
rules.basis: trade practice: each fixture's or room's water branch is teed off the nearest main of its system at right angles, the fixtures of one room and back-to-back rooms on one wet wall sharing one branch; a fixture branch nothing sizes is 1/2 inch (IPC Table 604.5)

rules.fills: a fixture's waste arm no plan joins to a drain line of its floor
rules.basis: trade practice: a fixture's waste arm runs from its trap to the nearest drain line of its floor at right angles and falls to it at the code's slope (IPC 704.1); it is the fixture's trap size (IPC Table 709.1: water closet 3 in., shower and urinal 2 in., clothes washer 2 in., tub, sink and laundry tray 1-1/2 in., lavatory 1-1/4 in.)

rules.fills: a fixture's vent no plan joins to a vent line or stack of its floor
rules.basis: trade practice: each fixture's trap is vented by a vent taken up its wet wall and over to the nearest vent line of its floor (IPC 901.2, 906.1 trap-to-vent distance); a vent is at least half its drain's size and not under 1-1/4 in. (IPC 916.2)

rules.fills: a branch circuit's raceway or cable path: the drawings show its devices and a homerun arrow, not the path
rules.basis: trade practice: a circuit's devices are joined device to device in a square tree above the ceiling, the homerun takes the corridor to its panel's top entry (rules: conduitroute.json; fill and box fill per NEC Ch. 9 and 314.16)

rules.fills: a circuit's route estimated from its homerun tag where the model could not route it
rules.basis: trade practice: a homerun the drawings mark by an arrow only is run along the plan's axes to its panel, a placeholder until it is routed

rules.fills: a power device no document puts on a circuit
rules.basis: trade practice: a device the documents leave off every circuit goes on a spare circuit of the nearest panel of its level, its homerun along the plan's axes in the ceiling space to the panel (NEC 210.11: every outlet is on a branch circuit)

rules.fills: an air terminal no duct of its system reaches
rules.basis: trade practice: each diffuser, register or grille is taken off the nearest duct of its system by a round branch at right angles at the duct's height, then down to the terminal at its neck size

rules.fills: a duct through a rated wall where the documents tag no damper
rules.basis: code: a duct penetrating a fire-resistance-rated assembly takes a fire damper (IMC 607.5); the field installs one at the wall in the duct's size; alternative: an exception of IMC 607.5 (a fire partition in a sprinklered building, a listed through-penetration) that the engineer may confirm instead

rules.fills: a return grille no return duct of its floor reaches
rules.basis: trade practice: a return grille the drawings leave unducted returns through the ceiling plenum to its unit (IMC 602 plenum); alternative: a ducted return the engineer may call for

rules.fills: a column the grid crossing implies where the plans draw none
rules.basis: trade practice: a structural grid crossing carries a column where the structural plans show the grid but no column outline

rules.fills: a raceway that meets another trade's duct or pipe, or another raceway, at its height where no tier of the ceiling space clears it
rules.basis: trade practice: the electrician offsets the raceway under the obstacle (over it where under would drop into the ceiling) with the clearance the routing keeps, a field offset at each side (rules: conduitroute.json clearances)

rules.fills: a panel whose allowed entry window can't take the raceways routed to it
rules.basis: trade practice: where a panel's top (or bottom) can't take its raceways, the electrician sets a pull box or wireway on it that they land in; an angle pull box is at least six times the largest raceway plus the others in the row (NEC 314.28(A)(2)); alternative: an extension gutter or a larger can

rules.fills: a product field the documents disagree on (the submittal against the schedule or the specification)
rules.basis: trade practice: the field installs what the approved submittal names; where it differs from the drawings' schedule or the specification, the schedule's value is kept beside it as the design value and the difference stays listed for the engineer

rules.fills: a device or junction box too small for what enters it (box fill)
rules.basis: code: a box's volume holds its conductors, devices, clamps and grounds by NEC 314.16(B); the field installs the next larger box of NEC Table 314.16(A), or adds an extension ring

rules.fills: two holes bored closer in one framing member than the hole rule allows
rules.basis: trade practice: holes in a member keep the maker's spacing (the hole rule's multiple of the larger hole); where two raceways would cross a member closer than that, the field bores one hole sized for both where the hole rule takes it at that distance from the bearing (NEC 300.4(A)(1) protection kept), else bores them a bay apart

rules.fills: a raceway too small for its conductors (fill over NEC Chapter 9 Table 1)
rules.basis: code: conductors fill at most 40 percent of a raceway of three or more (NEC Chapter 9 Table 1); the field pulls them in the next trade size that holds them (NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5)

rules.fills: branch conductors too small for their length (voltage drop over 3 percent)
rules.basis: code and practice: branch circuit conductors are sized for at most 3 percent voltage drop (NEC 210.19(A) Informational Note 4), the drawings' length table first; the field pulls the next conductor size
